E3 Detailed Design | Material Requirements and Purchasing Plan System
Page 1
Detailed Design of the Material Requirements and 
Purchasing Plan System
Experiment 3 | Technical draft v0.2 | 15 October 2026
This report refines the existing six-subsystem structured design into 14 selected procedures. It 
specifies input and output contracts, pseudocode, failure paths and implementation mappings, with 
two flowcharts, two Nassi-Shneiderman diagrams and two decision tables. The current 
implementation uses functions and records rather than a custom object-oriented model.
The group size is two, confirmed on 15 October 2026. E3 literally requires at least twice the number 
of group members in subsystems: six subsystems exceed the minimum of four. If the wording is 
intended to count refined modules instead, the 14 selected modules also exceed four. Member 
identities, actual division of work and the all-member review remain unrecorded; this is not yet a 
complete submission package.
Table 1.1 Scope inherited from E2
Subsystem Selected E3 modules
S1 Source maintenance M11, M14
S2 Snapshot and BOM validation M23
S3 Net requirements M30, M33
S4 Purchasing M40, M42, M43
S5 Dates and completion M50, M52, M53
S6 Publication and history M62, M63, M65
Sections 2 and 3 define records and procedures. Section 4 provides the two required model types. 
Sections 5 and 6 describe decisions and validation links. Section 7 reserves genuine submission 
records. All report content is in English as required by the supplied E3 brief; no FTP upload is 
performed.

E3 Detailed Design | Material Requirements and Purchasing Plan System
Page 2
2 Shared records and implementation boundaries
Table 2.1 Record contracts
Record Fields and ownership
SourceSet source_revision; materials, bom, stocks and tasks. Normalized copies retain 
immutable input provenance.
PlanningRequest request_id, selected_task_ids, baseline_date, rule_version. Selection IDs are 
canonicalized; execution order is separately priority-based.
PreparedContext Context snapshots, material/task indexes, graph adjacency/reachability/topological 
order and initial balances.
Demand and origin task, material, needed date, gross quantity; origins retain parent_demand_id, 
bom_path and contribution_qty.
Allocation and shortage Before/allocated/after balances; per-origin allocated/residual quantities; BUY 
shortage links to its demand.
Purchase bucket and 
surplus
Material/date, shortage IDs, gross gap, surplus used, residual gap, rounded quantity, 
order date and remaining lot quantities.
Outcome and saved 
document
VALID or INVALID, result/errors; saved_batch has immutable batch ID and UTC 
creation time. RISK does not imply INVALID.
Stable calculation IDs are compact JSON arrays, not delimiter-concatenated strings. Examples are 
["demand",task,material,date], ["origin",task,path] and ["purchase_bucket",material,date]. Root 
origins use ["root",task]. MAKE, shortage and allocation IDs retain their task/demand references. 
Batch IDs and source revision IDs are independently generated UUID hex values.
Implementation refinements from E2 are explicit: several logical leaf modules are inline steps; CSV 
imports replace whole selected tables; three SQLite tables store complete version documents instead 
of seven physical relational tables. The supported rule constant is checked, not dynamically selected 
by clients. History reads a stored result without recalculation.
Single warehouse, integer quantities and calendar days remain the current scope. The confirmed rule 
is task priority first, then due date, then ordinal ID. Neither calculation nor saving posts inventory. 
Current UI/CSV inputs are bounded to JavaScript safe integers; computed larger quantities retain 
exact decimal representation.

Page 3
3.1 M11 Parse and preview a CSV submission
E2 owner: S1. Implementation: csv_io.py:38-76 parse_table; csv_io.py:79-111 preview_import.
Input: current payload and one or more named CSV texts. Output: READY with a normalized 
candidate and row counts, or INVALID with located errors.
Precondition: a supported table name and UTF-8 text. The HTTP boundary caps the full JSON body 
at 2 MB. Each CSV is capped at 500,000 UTF-8 bytes and 5,000 records.
COPY the current payload to candidate
FOR each supplied table:
 CHECK exact header set, unique headers and row column counts
 PARSE integers; reject fractions, scientific notation or overflow
 DEFAULT blank minimum to 0 and blank purchase multiple to 1
 RECORD physical CSV ending-line numbers, including quoted newlines
 REPLACE that whole candidate table with the parsed rows
IF parsing errors exist: RETURN INVALID without applying candidate
REMEMBER old selected IDs that still occur in the new task table
SET candidate selection to all candidate tasks
CALL validate_and_prepare(candidate.sources, candidate.request)
IF invalid: remap row errors to CSV locations; RETURN INVALID
RESTORE surviving selected IDs in normalized candidate
RETURN READY(candidate, per-table counts)
Postcondition: no database or original input changes. The UI applies a valid preview explicitly; 
saving is a separate action. New task IDs are not selected automatically.
Failure paths: CSV_TYPE, CSV_HEADER, CSV_COLUMNS, CSV_INTEGER, CSV_SYNTAX, 
CSV_SIZE and business validation errors. Empty task data fails full validation. A changed editor/file 
invalidates the UI preview.
E2 refinement: M11 parsing and M12/M13 candidate preparation share this adapter. Current CSV 
semantics replace complete selected tables; they are not E2 upsert patches.

3.2 M14 Commit a source version
E2 owner: S1. Implementation: storage.py:60-90 save_workspace.
Input: database path, payload and expected_revision. Output: SAVED with normalized payload and 
new revision, INVALID, or CONFLICT.
Precondition: initialized schema. Validate copies before acquiring the write transaction. At least one 
valid task must exist; an empty saved selection is permitted.
COPY payload; remember whether its selection was empty
IF selection was empty: temporarily select all supplied tasks
VALIDATE and normalize the payload
VALIDATE again with every task selected, including unselected BOMs
IF either validation fails: RETURN INVALID
IF original selection was empty: restore the empty selection
CREATE revision ID and timestamp; put revision ID into sources
BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction
READ the current source_head revision (or null)
IF current differs from expected_revision:
 RETURN CONFLICT without inserting a revision
INSERT immutable source_revision with current as parent
INSERT or UPDATE source_head to the new revision
COMMIT transaction
RETURN SAVED only after successful commit
Invariant: a stale writer cannot move the head. A failed insert/head update/commit rolls back the 
whole transaction. This operation does not change actual stock or create a plan batch.
Database or filesystem failures propagate to the HTTP adapter, which returns 503 SAVE_FAILED. 
CONFLICT maps to HTTP 409; the browser retains its unsaved edits.
The actual connection context manages commit/rollback. BEGIN IMMEDIATE precedes the head 
comparison, so no writer can alter the head between comparison and update.

E3 Detailed Design | Material Requirements and Purchasing Plan System
Page 5
3.3 M23 Validate data and index the reachable BOM
E2 owner: S2. Implementation: planner.py:27-198 validate_and_prepare.
Input: sources and request records. Output: prepared context and an empty error list, or no context 
and blocking issues. This function also implements M22, M24 and M25.
Precondition: none for the public input shape. IDs are stripped and case-sensitive; quantities must be 
integers, not booleans. Request rule_version must match the supported constant.
COPY sources and request; validate records and nonempty selection
CHECK unique IDs, integer domains, valid dates and supply types
CHECK stock date = baseline and reserved <= on_hand
IF schema/field errors exist: RETURN no context and errors
BUILD adjacency; reject unknown references and duplicate edges
CHECK selected task IDs; sort each child list by ordinal ID
IF reference errors exist: RETURN no context and errors
COLLECT all reachable nodes from selected roots using a visited set
CHECK reachable stocks, MAKE children and BUY leaf restrictions
COMPUTE reachable indegrees; heap = zero-indegree nodes
WHILE heap is nonempty:
 REMOVE smallest node; append to topological order
 DECREMENT each child's indegree; enqueue newly zero children
IF order size differs from reachable size: add BOM_CYCLE issue
IF errors exist: RETURN no context and errors
SORT tasks by priority, due date, ordinal task ID
CANONICALIZE source rows; initialize on_hand - reserved balances
RETURN prepared snapshots, indexes, tasks, balances and graph
Postcondition: every reachable parent precedes its child. Validation includes branches covered by 
current stock; inventory cannot hide an illegal BOM. Only selected tasks enter calculation.
Cycle reporting lists nodes blocked by topological sorting; this can include descendants of a cycle 
and is not a reconstructed cycle path. Row locations in JSON are zero-based.
Global field/reference checks cover all supplied rows. MAKE completeness, BUY children, missing 
stock and cycle checks apply to the selected reachable graph; save/import select all tasks for their 
extra validation.

E3 Detailed Design | Material Requirements and Purchasing Plan System
Page 6
3.4 M30 Calculate net multilevel requirements
E2 owner: S3. Implementation: planner.py:208-256 net_requirements.
Input: validated prepared context. Output: NetBundle with demands, allocations, MAKE lines, BUY 
shortages and final balances, or date-range errors.
Precondition: valid acyclic reachable graph, sorted tasks and matching stock snapshots. Balances are 
private to one batch and shared across its tasks.
COPY initial balances once; initialize output collections
FOR each task in priority, due date, ordinal ID order:
 SEED pending[root][due_date] with the root contribution
 FOR material in parent-before-child topological order:
 FOR needed_date in sorted pending[material] dates:
 SORT origins by BOM path then origin ID; SUM gross demand
 CALL M33; install new balance; retain demand and ledger
 IF net quantity = 0: CONTINUE to next date bucket
 KEEP residual origins with residual_qty > 0
 IF BUY: append shortage and CONTINUE
 CALL M52 for the MAKE start date
 IF date error: RETURN no bundle and located errors
 APPEND a MAKE line for the net quantity
 FOR child edge in child-ID order:
 FOR residual origin in fixed source order:
 child qty = residual_qty * edge.qty_per
 EXTEND path; reference parent demand; create stable ID
 APPEND contribution to pending[child][start_date]
RETURN bundle with final balances
Invariants: same-task/material/date origins merge before allocation; all parents feed a child before it 
is processed. Only residual MAKE demand creates child demand. No cross-task reuse of temporary 
pending buckets.
M32 merging, M34 expansion, M35 shortage recording and M36 assembly are inline steps, not 
separate Python functions. A date error discards the partial bundle; no actual inventory is posted.
Path records can grow much faster than node count in densely shared graphs. Do not describe full 
expansion complexity as merely linear in BOM nodes and edges.

E3 Detailed Design | Material Requirements and Purchasing Plan System
Page 7
3.5 M33 Allocate stock and attribute it to sources
E2 owner: S3. Implementation: core.py:24-85 allocate_stock.
Input: demand and balance for one material. Output: netted_demand, allocation ledger and a new 
balance. No caller-owned record is mutated.
Precondition: positive gross quantity; nonnegative available stock; valid date; nonempty uniquely 
identified origins with valid paths and positive contributions summing to gross.
VALIDATE quantities, date, material match and origin records
allocated = MIN(available, gross)
after = available - allocated
remaining = allocated; source_allocations = empty list
FOR origin sorted by ordinal BOM path then origin ID:
 taken = MIN(remaining, origin.contribution_qty)
 residual = origin.contribution_qty - taken
 APPEND origin ID, taken and residual
 remaining = remaining - taken
CREATE ledger with before, allocated, after and copied attribution
CREATE copied demand with allocated and net = gross - allocated
RETURN demand, ledger and copied balance set to after
Postconditions: gross = allocated + net; before = allocated + after; after >= 0. Source allocations sum 
to allocated; source residuals sum to net. The attribution remainder ends at zero.
An invalid leaf precondition raises ValueError. The public planner validates source data before 
constructing this leaf input; internal invariant failures must not be reported as successful plans.
Example: origins 7 and 5, available 8 gives origin allocations 7 and 1; residuals 0 and 4; net demand 
4. Attribution order is independent of the original input row order.

E3 Detailed Design | Material Requirements and Purchasing Plan System
Page 8
3.6 M40 Plan purchases by material and date
E2 owner: S4. Implementation: planner.py:259-300 plan_purchases.
Input: NetBundle and validated material index. Output: envelope containing purchase buckets, 
surplus-use records and final positive surplus lots, or located date errors.
Precondition: priority-based existing-stock allocation has finished. Purchase surplus is a separate 
planned supply pool; it is not available stock.
GROUP BUY shortages by material and needed_date
INITIALIZE empty pools, buckets and surplus-use records
FOR group in material-ID then needed-date order:
 CREATE stable bucket ID; gross = SUM shortage quantities
 CALL M42 on this material's eligible earlier lots; obtain gap
 CALL M43(gap, minimum_qty, purchase_multiple)
 SET order_date to null
 IF purchase_qty > 0:
 CALL M52(needed_date, purchase lead time)
 IF error: RETURN no envelope and located errors
 IF purchase_qty > gap: ADD surplus lot at needed_date
 RECORD reasons for used surplus, minimum and multiple rounding
 APPEND bucket with sorted shortage IDs and remaining surplus
RETURN envelope and only positive final surplus lots
Postcondition: same-date shortages share one rounding decision. A zero-order bucket remains 
available for explanation but does not count as a procurement suggestion.
No purchase start event exists for quantity zero. Invalid date arithmetic blocks the full plan; merely 
early dates become risks later in M50/M53.
The current surplus pool is local mutable state owned by M40. The returned NetBundle is retained as 
input context and is not modified by the purchase stage.

E3 Detailed Design | Material Requirements and Purchasing Plan System
Page 9
3.7 M42 Consume eligible planned surplus
E2 owner: S4. Implementation: planner.py:259-300 plan_purchases.
Input: current material pool, demand bucket ID/date and gross shortage. Output: residual gap and use 
records, with this local pool reduced.
Precondition: caller processes each material in ascending need date. Lots carry source bucket ID, 
arrival date and remaining quantity. This logical module is inline in M40.
gap = gross_shortage
FOR lot sorted by arrival_date then source_bucket_ID:
 IF lot.arrival_date <= needed_date
 AND gap > 0 AND lot.remaining_qty > 0:
 used = MIN(gap, lot.remaining_qty)
 lot.remaining_qty = lot.remaining_qty - used
 gap = gap - used
 APPEND source bucket, demand bucket, used,
 source arrival date and use date
RETURN gap and accumulated use records
Invariant: gross_shortage = surplus_used + gap; gap and all lot balances stay nonnegative. No lot 
later than the demand can supply it, including when that lot belongs to a higher-priority task.
A zero gap or exhausted lot takes the no-consumption branch. Lots do not survive into another 
planning batch. Earlier theoretical arrivals may still carry execution risk; the calculation does not 
guarantee on-time delivery.
Example: a 30-unit purchase for a gap of 23 creates 7 units. A later gap of 7 consumes that surplus 
and orders zero. Reversing dates does not allow the later lot to supply the earlier gap.

E3 Detailed Design | Material Requirements and Purchasing Plan System
Page 10
3.8 M43 Round the purchase quantity
E2 owner: S4. Implementation: core.py:88-97 round_purchase_qty.
Input: remaining_gap, minimum_qty and purchase_multiple. Output: exact integer purchase quantity. 
This is a pure leaf function.
Precondition: gap and minimum are nonnegative integers, multiple is a positive integer; booleans are 
not accepted as integer quantities.
VALIDATE integer domains
IF remaining_gap = 0:
 RETURN 0
target = MAX(remaining_gap, minimum_qty)
lot_count = (target + purchase_multiple - 1) DIV purchase_multiple
RETURN lot_count * purchase_multiple
Postcondition: a positive result is at least both gap and minimum, is divisible by the multiple, and is 
the smallest such multiple. Zero gap always orders zero even when the minimum is positive.
Invalid domain values raise ValueError. DIV means exact integer division; floating-point ceilings are 
not used. This preserves exactness for large computed quantities.
Examples: gap 620, minimum 100, multiple 100 gives 700; gap 0 with the same minimum gives 0. 
The decision table in Section 5 separates the zero, minimum and divisibility cases.

E3 Detailed Design | Material Requirements and Purchasing Plan System
Page 11
3.9 M50 Complete the calculated outcome
E2 owner: S5. Implementation: planner.py:303-326 calculate_plan.
Input: sources and request. Output: VALID with a complete result and no errors, or INVALID with 
no result and blocking issues. This boundary does not perform I/O.
Precondition: public callers may supply malformed input; validate_and_prepare handles schema and 
business validation. The supported rule version is prototype-v0.2.
CREATE INVALID skeleton with request ID when available
CALL M23 to validate and prepare
IF errors: RETURN INVALID with errors
CALL M30 for net requirements
IF errors: RETURN INVALID with errors
CALL M40 for purchase planning
IF errors: RETURN INVALID with errors
COLLECT every selected task due-date event
ADD each nonzero MAKE start event
ADD each nonzero purchase order-date event
CALL M53 using the request baseline
COUNT tasks, MAKE lines, positive purchase lines and risks
RETURN VALID(result including risks, summary and snapshots)
Postcondition: a blocking failure never exposes a partial valid result. A result with scheduling risks is 
still VALID and preserves its original computed dates.
Every selected task due date is checked, including a task fully covered by finished-goods stock. 
Summary purchase count excludes zero-order surplus-consumption buckets.
E2 M50 coordination, M51 event collection and M54 assembly are combined here; netting and 
purchase work remain explicit function calls. Saving belongs to M62.

E3 Detailed Design | Material Requirements and Purchasing Plan System
Page 12
3.10 M52 Subtract calendar lead time
E2 owner: S5. Implementation: core.py:100-117 subtract_calendar_days.
Input: needed_date in strict YYYY-MM-DD form and nonnegative integer lead_days. Output: OK 
with ISO date, or ERROR with a DATE_RANGE issue.
Precondition: valid calendar date and integer lead time. Dates use calendar days, including weekends 
and holidays; no shop calendar or capacity model is applied.
VALIDATE integer lead_days and strict ISO date
TRY:
 start = parsed needed_date - duration(lead_days)
CATCH date arithmetic overflow:
 RETURN ERROR(value=null, DATE_RANGE blocking issue)
RETURN OK(value=start as YYYY-MM-DD, no issues)
Postcondition: zero lead leaves the date unchanged. A valid computed date before the baseline 
remains a date; it is not a DATE_RANGE error and will be assessed by M53.
Invalid date syntax/domain raises ValueError at the leaf; arithmetic overflow returns a structured 
error. planner.required_start attaches task/material/location context to that error.
Examples: 2026-10-10 minus 2 days is 2026-10-08; 2024-03-01 minus 1 day is 2024-02-29. An 
unrepresentable result before year 1 is a blocking range failure.

E3 Detailed Design | Material Requirements and Purchasing Plan System
Page 13
3.11 M53 Flag dates before the planning baseline
E2 owner: S5. Implementation: core.py:120-137 flag_early_dates.
Input: required event records and baseline_date. Output: a list of RISK issues with event references, 
original dates and days before baseline.
Precondition: validated baseline and event dates. M50 provides task due dates and only required 
nonzero production/purchase starts.
PARSE baseline; risks = empty list
FOR event in required_events:
 PARSE event.date
 IF event.date < baseline:
 APPEND EARLY_REQUIRED_DATE issue with severity RISK
 STORE event ID, task/material references and original date
 STORE days_before_baseline = baseline - event.date in days
RETURN risks
Invariant: the issue set contains exactly the supplied events strictly before baseline. Dates equal to 
baseline are allowed. Inputs are neither shifted nor rewritten.
Invalid event dates raise ValueError at the leaf. A RISK is not a blocking issue: the UI may show 
theoretical quantities and dates while warning that timely execution is not established.
Example: event 2026-10-09 and baseline 2026-10-10 gives one risk with 1 day; event 2026-10-10 
gives no risk. Tests of risk decisions belong to E4/E5, not a claim of capacity feasibility.

E3 Detailed Design | Material Requirements and Purchasing Plan System
Page 14
3.12 M62 Calculate and atomically save a plan
E2 owner: S6. Implementation: storage.py:93-111 calculate_and_save.
Input: initialized database and payload. Output: calculated INVALID result, or VALID result plus 
saved_batch ID/time only after commit.
Precondition: database schema available. Every submission receives an independent immutable input 
snapshot; saving a plan does not save the editor workspace.
COPY payload; create batch ID and timestamp
IF payload is a record with sources:
 SET source_revision to batch-input- followed by batch ID
CALL M50 on the copied sources and request
IF result is INVALID: RETURN it without database writes
ASSEMBLE document with outcome and saved_batch metadata
OPEN connection and transactional context
INSERT one plan_batch row containing:
 ID, time, baseline, ordered task IDs, summary, full JSON document
COMMIT transaction
RETURN outcome with saved_batch metadata
ON storage failure: roll back and propagate to HTTP adapter
Postcondition: a successful history row includes the same sources, rules, allocations, demands, 
purchase decisions and risks used in the calculation. No half-plan is advertised as saved.
HTTP application catches SQLite/OSError failures and returns 503 SAVE_FAILED. The batch-input 
source_revision is an embedded provenance token, not a foreign key into source_revision.
E2 logical seven-table responsibilities are implemented with three physical tables and complete 
JSON documents. SQLite triggers reject UPDATE/DELETE of batch/version rows through the 
application database.

E3 Detailed Design | Material Requirements and Purchasing Plan System
Page 15
3.13 M63 Read immutable planning history
E2 owner: S6. Implementation: storage.py:114-120 list_batches; storage.py:123-126 get_batch.
Input: database plus list offset/limit or a batch ID. Output: summary items and next_offset, a 
complete saved document, or None for a missing batch.
Precondition: initialized database. HTTP validates nonnegative list offsets. Listing is ordered by 
created_at descending, then batch_id descending.
FOR a history list request:
 SELECT limit + 1 summary rows at the requested offset
 DECODE task IDs and summary JSON for the first limit rows
 SET next_offset if the extra row exists; otherwise null
 RETURN items and next_offset
FOR a batch detail request:
 SELECT document WHERE batch_id equals the bound parameter
 IF missing: RETURN None
 DECODE and RETURN the stored document without recalculating
Postcondition: history reflects the original snapshot even if the editor or saved workspace changes. 
Viewing history does not replace the current editor data.
The HTTP detail route maps None to 404. Storage failures map to 503. Offset pagination can shift if 
new batches are inserted between page reads; it is not a pinned snapshot cursor.
Current scope is read-only history, with a version token to discard stale asynchronous UI responses. 
Restoring historical inputs into the editor is not implemented or claimed here.

E3 Detailed Design | Material Requirements and Purchasing Plan System
Page 16
3.14 M65 Export a selected saved plan to CSV
E2 owner: S6. Implementation: csv_io.py:123-151 export_batch; csv_io.py:25-31 encode_csv.
Input: saved batch document and MAKE, PURCHASE, ALLOCATION, TRACE or RISK kind. 
Output: UTF-8 BOM CSV bytes with batch_id in every data row.
Precondition: saved record has a valid outcome. HTTP loads the selected immutable batch and 
validates the export kind before calling this adapter.
READ result and batch ID only from the supplied saved record
SELECT columns and rows for the requested export kind
FOR TRACE rows:
 JOIN each origin to its allocation by origin_id
 ENCODE BOM paths as JSON within the CSV field
FOR PURCHASE rows: encode shortage ID lists as JSON
PREFIX batch_id to every data row
WRITE full header, even when there are no data rows
FOR each row:
 PREFIX dangerous spreadsheet text with an apostrophe
 USE CSV writer quoting for commas, quotes and newlines
RETURN UTF-8 BOM bytes with CRLF record separators
Postcondition: exported amounts and dates come from the selected batch, not current input. Large 
Python integers are serialized as exact decimal text; spreadsheet auto-conversion may require 
importing those columns as text.
Unsupported kinds raise ValueError internally and are rejected with HTTP 400 at the route. 
Unknown batches return 404. Formula protection covers leading whitespace before =, +, -, @ and 
designated control/apostrophe prefixes.
The result response separately encodes integers beyond JavaScript safe range as decimal strings. 
Input CSV integers are restricted to 9007199254740991; this restriction is not applied to already￾computed Python result quantities.

5 Business decision tables
The following tables partition valid inputs or ordered control outcomes. They supplement the 
pseudocode; they do not authorize changes to the confirmed priority-first inventory policy.
Table 5.1 Purchase quantity rules for M43
Rule Conditions Action
R1 gap = 0 Return 0; ignore positive minimum.
R2 0 < gap < minimum; minimum divisible by multiple Return minimum.
R3 0 < gap < minimum; minimum not divisible Round minimum up to the next multiple.
R4 gap > 0 and gap >= minimum; gap divisible Return gap.
R5 gap > 0 and gap >= minimum; gap not divisible Round gap up to the next multiple.
Invalid 
domain
Negative/fractional input, boolean, or multiple <= 0 Reject before R1-R5; ValueError at leaf.
Table 5.2 Ordered publication decisions
Priority Condition Result and persistence
1 Blocking validation/calculation issue INVALID; no plan row.
2 Calculation valid, storage operation fails HTTP 503 SAVE_FAILED; no claimed 
successful save.
3 Calculation valid, commit succeeds, risks exist VALID with RISK records and saved ID; 
preserve dates.
4 Calculation valid, commit succeeds, no risks VALID with empty risk list and saved ID.
Workspace conflicts are separate from batch publication: an expected source revision mismatch 
produces CONFLICT/HTTP 409 before source insertion. New plan batches may still be computed 
from an explicit unsaved payload, because they preserve that submitted snapshot independently.

The E3 verification record records document structure, code anchors, source hashes, diagram files 
and independent contract walkthroughs executed for this report. Existing suite files are evidence 
pointers, not a claim that those suites were rerun for a documentation change. E3 does not establish 
all five E4 coverage criteria or a complete E5 black-box report.
Independent walkthrough expectations include stock origins 7 and 5 against stock 8; purchase gaps 
620 and 0 under a minimum of 100 and multiple 100; leap-day subtraction; baseline equality; and the 
multilevel example A=100, B=180, D purchase=620. The checker compares these with current 
functions and records actual values.
Important limits remain: dense DAGs can produce many explicit origin paths; full history documents 
can be large; offset history pagination is not a stable concurrent cursor. No automatic historical-input 
restoration, capacity scheduling, supplier confirmation, multi-warehouse netting or real inventory 
posting is claimed.
